newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK pledges to protect copyrights after handover.
newsitem.headline: HK pledges to protect copyrights after handover.

text.p: Hong Kong pledged on Thursday to maintain a strong system to protect intellectual property rights (IPR) after the territory's handover to China on July 1.

"We are particularly concerned to ensure that Customs has sufficient powers to enforce effectively against copyright piracy," Stephen Selby, director of Hong Kong's Intellectual Property Department, told a news conference.
Selby did not specify what other action Customs and Excise would take.

Rampant copyright piracy in China's booming southern province of Guangdong, involving laser and compact discs as well as computer software, brought China and Washington to the brink of a multibillion-dollar trade war last June.
Washington has said it worries Hong Kong, which borders Guangdong, was the probable spigot through which pirated goods made in China pour into international markets.
Some 250,000 trucks move across the border every day with Chinese goods for export, and customs officials have said that checking each one was an impossible task.
Hong Kong was fully committed to IPR protection, Selby said, adding that authorities forged closer ties with their Chinese counterparts last year to combat piracy.
Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30 after more than 150 years as a British colony.
